documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Maternal-fetal medicine office called for our records ahead of pt's delivery planning (problem list, med list, 2025 TCM note, 2/2025 echo). Release on file from pt dated 7/2025. Faxed 14 pages, confirmation received.

events.reason: Dyspnea and seizures after delivery before arrival

reports.text: Bedside point-of-care study during resuscitation. Left ventricle with normal systolic function. Right ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function; no septal flattening. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of right heart strain.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 03/19/2026; date of service 03/10/2026)

CC: shortness of breath and seizure after delivery.

HPI: 34 y/o G3, term, brought in by EMS about half an hour after a rapid spontaneous vaginal delivery before arrival (liveborn infant). Shortly after the birth she became acutely dyspneic and had seizures witnessed by EMS. Background of chronic hypertension on labetalol, a placental abruption in 2023, and amniotic fluid embolism after her delivery in 01/2025.
Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis) - latex-free room.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin with DHA, folic acid 1 mg.

Exam: BP 70/40, HR 120, RR 30, SpO2 85% on room air. Not protecting her airway. Rales throughout both lung fields. Petechiae across the chest and both arms.

Course: intubated for airway protection. Labs: Hgb 9.0 g/dL (ref 12-16), platelets 50K (ref 150-400K), PT 18 s (ref 12-15), aPTT 40 s (ref 30-40), fibrinogen 100 mg/dL (ref 200-400), D-dimer elevated. Bedside echo: no right heart strain. Aggressive crystalloid and blood product resuscitation, yet she continued to decline. OB and critical care at bedside.

Impression: recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with disseminated intravascular coagulation and hypovolemic shock.
Disposition: ICU.

events.reason: Recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and shock

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 03/19/2026)
Admitted 03/10/2026 via the ED. Discharged 03/18/2026.

Principal diagnosis: amniotic fluid embolism, recurrent (prior episode 01/2025).
Secondary: disseminated intravascular coagulation; hypovolemic shock.
Background: chronic hypertension; anxiety disorder; placental abruption 10/2023 with emergency cesarean; laparoscopic appendectomy.
Allergies: sulfonamides - rash; latex - contact dermatitis.

Hospital course: Arrived intubated from the ED after a precipitous term delivery before arrival, with hypoxemia, seizures, shock and consumptive coagulopathy. In the ICU, resuscitation with blood products continued until bleeding and coagulation studies corrected; blood pressure recovered over the first day. No further seizure activity. Extubated 03/12 without difficulty. Moved to the postpartum unit 03/14 and progressed well. Hemoglobin stable on the last two checks before discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged): labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.

Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with CBC, CMP and coagulation studies; obstetric postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM outreach, discharged yesterday after second amniotic fluid embolism (ICU 3/10, extubated 3/12). Spoke with pt. Breathing OK at rest, gets winded on the stairs but improving. Light bleeding, no clots. No bruising or gum bleeding. No seizures since the hospital. Taking labetalol, PNV, folic acid; no new prescriptions. Tearful at times on the call, says it is a lot. Booked TCM with PCP 3/24 with labs. Reviewed ED precautions.

events.reason: Transitional care visit after ICU admission

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM, discharged 3/18. ED record and discharge summary reviewed.

What happened: precipitous term delivery 3/10 before reaching the hospital; within minutes dyspnea and seizures, arrived hypotensive 70/40, sat 85%, rales, petechiae. Plt 50K, fibrinogen 100, PT 18, Hgb 9. Bedside echo without RV strain (different from 2025). Recurrent AFE with DIC and hypovolemic shock. Intubated, products, extubated 3/12, home 3/18. Baby born alive.

Now: two weeks postpartum. Stairs easier each day. No chest pain, no bleeding beyond light lochia, no bruising. No more seizures. Tired. She cries when she talks about it and said she thought she wasn't going to wake up this time. Still declines medication; says talking with me and her OB helps.

Meds unchanged: labetalol 200 mg BID, PNV w/ DHA, folic acid 1 mg. Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 normal RA. Pale-ish, tired, appropriate. No petechiae now. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear, no rales. Abdomen soft, nontender. Calves soft, no edema. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 9.

A/P
1. Recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and hypovolemic shock - recovered; resolved. CBC, CMP, PT/INR today.
2. Postpartum Hgb - recheck today, then in about 6 weeks.
3. Chronic HTN - office BP a bit high today, home readings 120s-130s/80s; continue labetalol 200 BID and recheck in May.
4. Anxiety disorder - worse after this. Supportive visit; will see her in May and sooner by portal if needed.
Med rec done, no changes.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tessa - hemoglobin is 10.2, which is good recovery from 9 in the ED, and your platelets, clotting tests, kidney and liver numbers are all normal now. No iron needed; your blood count should keep coming up. We'll check it again in May.

documents.title: Leave form again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Third time doing this form, at least I know the drill. Leave administrator needs the medical portion for the hospitalization, with an expected return in mid-June. Attached. Thank you.

documents.title: RE: Leave form again
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Done - PCP filled out the medical portion with an expected return date of 6/15. Faxed this morning and copy saved to your chart.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Tessa Turcotte was seen on 04/22/2026 for her postpartum visit after delivery on 03/10/2026 complicated by recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and shock requiring ICU care. She is recovering well. Lochia has resolved and her exam is unremarkable. Blood pressure is controlled on labetalol 200 mg twice daily, which remains under your management.

Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).

Thank you for sharing her care.

Obstetrics

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after the March admission. OB postpartum letter reviewed. Energy is mostly back. Walking most days, no dyspnea. No seizures. Planning to go back to work 6/15.
HTN: home readings 120s-130s/80s, labetalol 200 BID, still on PNV and folate.
Anxiety: GAD-7 7, down from 9. Sleeping better as the baby does.
Exam: vitals as charted. Color better. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: Postpartum anemia - CBC today, expect near baseline. Chronic HTN controlled, continue. Anxiety disorder improving. Physical and Pap in July.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is back to your normal of 12, and platelets are normal. Nothing else needed for this.

reports.text: Specimen: liquid-based cervical cytology. Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual + Pap. Back at work a month, part of the week from home.

Interval: 3/2026 precipitous term delivery complicated by recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and hypovolemic shock, ICU, recovered. Hgb back to 12 in May. OB postpartum visit 4/22 fine.

HTN: home 120s-130s/80s, labetalol 200 BID. Still on PNV with DHA and folic acid.
Anxiety: GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 2. Better than spring; occasional bad nights.
ROS negative.

PMH: chronic HTN; anxiety disorder; placental abruption 2023; amniotic fluid embolism 2025 and 2026 with DIC.
PSH: lap appendectomy 2015; emergency C/S 10/2023.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID; PNV w/ DHA daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa (rash); latex (contact dermatitis).
SH: HR coordinator. Former smoker, quit 2019. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month.
FH: mother preeclampsia and chronic HTN, father HTN, maternal aunt placental abruption.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT normal, thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts: no masses, no skin changes. Abdomen soft, nontender, transverse scar healed. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal, Pap with HPV collected with latex-free speculum and gloves. No edema. Skin normal.

A/P
- HM: Pap with HPV sent. CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and COVID in the fall.
- Chronic HTN: controlled on labetalol, continue. Recheck in October.
- Anxiety disorder: stable/improving, no meds.
- History of abruption and recurrent AFE: on the problem history.
RTC October for BP.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tessa, your Pap is normal and HPV negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Blood count, kidney and liver tests, and cholesterol are all normal. See you in October.
